description: An Electrician was working on an ESD push station when the facility suffered an ESD and total power loss. The emergency generator did not start as designed per the cause and effect according to the PIC. Power was restored at 12:59PM and production was restarted at 2:10PM. The seawater (firewater) pumps are electric driven and do not run on an independent drive. The pumps are powered from the platform 480V bus which is normally powered by the turbine generator and with the backup diesel generator. During the total power loss period of 15 minutes, all hydrocarbon production was automatically shut down (including up and over pipeline) and the facility had whatever sweater pressure was left in the system. The Enchilada facility does have manual override capability to start the backup generator for firewater supply. However, since there was no fire alarm when the event occurred, the platform personnel utilized the time to confirm there is no real manual initial emergency before resetting and starting to restore power. There was no loss comm to Well and Safety System. CCTV was working and Platform UPS power remain energized during the event. The root cause is due to ghost wiring issue from the generator water mist upgrade project. Same exact event occurred during commissioning of the project and claimed to be corrected. description: 09.15.2023: As required by 30 CFR 250.188(b)(3), Talos Energy Ventures LLC submits the initial/final notification of an unplanned muster event that occurred on EW-873 "Lobster" (G12136) at 11:45 hours on 09/13/2023. Root Cause: The Automation Technician failed to properly code the TSE loop in his software upgrade. The system was tested again and functioned properly, the guard was reinstalled, the gas test passed before entry.

description: A small flame was witnessed by two personnel on the turbo insulation blanket of compressor at our SM 99A facility. The flame was quickly extinguished by one personnel using a nearby water hose. It should be noted that the water hose used was utility water and not part of the fire water system. Although no damage was identified by the flame, the initial investigation revealed that a bracket, which helps support the expansion joint for the turbo, had broken. The resulting vibration caused the expansion joint to crack, and once it cracked, the hot exhaust contacted the exhaust's blanket. This led to oily/coolant residue on the exhaust's blanket to flame. There were no injuries resulting from this incident and current POB at the facility is 14. The facility remains on-line however, the compressor was shut-in and will remain shut-in until repairs are made. Initial first report was made to BSEE Lafayette afterhours line. Update 8/28: Upon further investigation, it has been determined that the exhaust's expansion joint does not have a crack. However, oil residue was found on the blanket, and it was determined that the heat from the exhaust caused this residue to ignite. Extensive maintenance was conducted on the compressor prior to the incident, which involved replacing the turbo. It is believed that either oil from the replaced turbo or coolant during maintenance became the source of the residue on the exhaust's blanket. As a result, both the expansion joint and the exhaust blanket have been replaced. We are confident that we have successfully eliminated the cause of this incident.
